title: Ben Johnson: 'We have to play the best we've played all year' on Monday night | Press Conference
headline: Kyle Monangai is out Monday and Colston Loveland is expected to practice, while Zavier Scott should see more backfield work.
summary: Johnson said Kyle Monangai, who did not practice this week, should be counted out for Monday night, and he is hopeful the back can return sooner rather than later. He said Colston Loveland is listed on the injury report but he hopes it is minor and expects him to practice that day. Zavier Scott has been getting more practice reps and playing time over the last few weeks, and Johnson said Scott could see more carries, with all three backs needed. Theo Benedet is starting at left tackle. Johnson said the team will need a clean game with no turnovers or penalties in a hostile road environment against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. He also addressed the newly acquired defensive lineman, saying he expects the player's impact to be significant, though the transcript garbles his name and he may not play at his normal snap load in Week 1. Johnson also commented on Caleb Williams' cleats situation, saying he is all about the team and will not hurt it.

The transcript garbles his name, so it was not attributed to a roster player. Johnson said he's still learning the system and may not carry his normal snap load in Week 1.
Johnson was asked about the cleats issue and said Williams is all about the team and will not hurt it. Johnson said the team has been in daily contact with the GM about the situation.
Johnson praised Dennis Allen's creativity and said the new defensive acquisition will help mask weaknesses elsewhere on defense and elevate the group.
Johnson said the team has less high-end draft capital going forward but still believes in its draft and development process, and that practice squad players are ready to contribute.
Johnson emphasized clean play, avoiding turnovers and penalties, and communication in a loud road environment; he called Seattle well-coached across all three phases.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 8 vs. Bears
headline: Charbonnet has a set usage plan and is expected to play, Shaheed is out this week, and Josh Jones starts at left tackle while Drake Thomas starts at linebacker.
summary: Macdonald said the team has a plan for Zach Charbonnet's usage in this game, though it may shift during play. He called Charbonnet a three-down back who catches out of the backfield, runs a full route tree, handles every rushing situation, and has been excellent in pass protection, and he praised the speed of Charbonnet's return from injury. Rashid Shaheed is progressing well but will miss this game, with his status to be reassessed next week. Macdonald confirmed Josh Jones will start at left tackle, citing his strong play when filling in last season, and he praised Quenton Nelson's poise and confidence as he settles in after a few days with the team. The offensive line has been reshuffled with new starters at left tackle, left guard and right guard, and the staff is working through how much of the new scheme to use. Drake Thomas will start, with Tyrice Knight having played well in his absence, though Macdonald said the team is willing to play both together. Any roster move involving a player not on the injury report would come Monday and be handled through transactions. Macdonald also said Tory Horton is getting more opportunity and he expects him to take advantage of it. He praised George Holani as an underrated pass blocker, and said Grey Zabel is handling a demotion-type change well.
